content:
zoe: ACME reports intermittent 503s overnight (~01:10-02:30 UTC). They can repro ~1/3 attempts. Correlates with regional routing config push. Asking for triage @mike @elena :rotating_light:

mike: On it. Can you paste a request_id + example curl so I can replay?

zoe: sample req_ids: rq_20260317_01_0134, rq_20260317_01_2045, rq_20260317_01_3152. customer repro curl:

zoe: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

support-bot: Incident INC-1267 created (severity: high) and routed to SRE oncall.

mike: Observing 503 spike on proxy edge around same window. LB shows 504s to backend pool intermittently. Attaching quick tail of proxy logs:

mike: ```
2026-03-17T01:12:03Z proxy[edge-usw2] INFO req=rq_20260317_01_0134 backend=10.2.3.5 status=502 -> client=503
2026-03-17T01:12:03Z proxy[edge-usw2] WARN conn=1789 streams_active=120 window=0
2026-03-17T01:12:44Z proxy[edge-usw2] INFO req=rq_20260317_01_2045 backend=10.2.3.6 status=200
2026-03-17T01:22:10Z proxy[edge-eu] INFO req=rq_20260317_01_3152 backend=10.3.4.7 status=503
```

elena: Hm, the "streams_active=120 window=0" line looks like HTTP/2 flow control exhaustion. We rolled out multiplexing for higher throughput at 00:55 UTC in two regions. @james did the rollout include keepalive/stream-window changes?

james: I rolled the feature flag edge-multiplex=enabled at 00:55 UTC to canary -> 2/3 regions. No keepalive changes in that rollout. Reverting now to disable multiplex on the canary set.

james: Revert completed at 01:45 UTC for canary cohort. Rolling forward stop; monitoring.

sre-bot: Alert: svc/proxy p95 latency increased 120% (01:00-02:00 UTC).

mike: Repro steps I used: spawn 50 concurrent short-lived HTTP/2 streams from a single host with the same Authorization token. ~30% of runs returned 503. When I lowered multiplexing concurrency to 8 streams per connection the failures vanish. Workaround for customers: reduce per-connection concurrency or use separate connections.

zoe: Draft customer update: "Sorry for the disruption. We discovered an interaction between our new HTTP/2 multiplexing rollout and some client patterns that can exhaust stream windowing, causing 503s. We reverted the rollout for affected regions at 01:45 UTC and are monitoring. Please retry; if you still see failures send us a sample request_id. We can route your traffic to a dedicated pool temporarily." Approve to send?

elena: LGTM. Root cause summary: multiplexing + keepalive/flow-control edge mismatch + K/V cache lock contention under high stream fan-in. Next actions: (1) add e2e test for high-stream fan-in, (2) tune initial window/keepalive, (3) add circuit-breaker for per-conn streams, (4) follow-up postmortem. I'm starting a canary fix that adjusts window and enforces a per-connection stream limit.

mike: Mitigation applied: pinned ACME to dedicated routing pool in us-west-2 to avoid shared edge for the next 24h. No billing impact planned but tagging usage for follow-up.

support_lead: I'll send the customer note now and offer to walk through repro. If INC-1267 is >1h we'll schedule a postmortem. Great triage.

zoe: Sent update to ACME (included rollback window, what to try, and request_id ask). Customer acknowledged and will retest this morning.

mike: I'll keep monitoring logs for 2h. If we see reoccurrence we'll rollback further and throttle multiplex rollout.

zoe: Closing thread for now—will re-open if ACME reports further failures. :thumbsup:
